summary:
The National Capital Region stands under the national framework of the Philippines: national law on legal gender recognition, anti-discrimination, detention placement and marriage applies here as it does elsewhere in the country. The layer specific to this region is municipal.

Quezon City has enacted an ordinance, sponsored by Councilor Bernard Herrera and colleagues, requiring every city public health facility to provide gender-affirming consultations and counselling, mental health support, and medical guidance and referrals irrespective of a patient's gender identity or expression. Mayor Joy Belmonte said the measure removes longstanding healthcare barriers for gender-diverse and transgender residents. The obligation attaches to city-run facilities, so its reach is municipal rather than regional.

Trans-specific violence in the region is documented. Shaina Bayabay, 29, was killed in Pasig City on 1 March 2024; the recorded cause is strangulation, and the underlying report states she was killed during a drinking session. The inventory records this as a single case and supplies no regional count or rate against which to read it.
tangentialFactors: The Quezon City ordinance is the only municipal measure in the inventory that addresses trans healthcare access in the National Capital Region. No comparable measure in another Metro Manila local government unit appears in the sources. As described, the ordinance covers city public health facilities; the inventory records no extension of the obligation to private hospitals or clinics, which remain governed by the national patchwork rather than by city policy.
localsOnly: For residents of Quezon City, the ordinance creates an entitlement to gender-affirming consultations, counselling, mental health support and referrals at city public health facilities, without regard to gender identity or expression. Residents elsewhere in the National Capital Region fall outside that entitlement unless their own local government has adopted an equivalent measure, which the inventory does not record.
outOfScopeNotes: The inventory does not record how the Quezon City ordinance is enforced, what budget or staffing supports it, or whether any complaint of refusal at a city facility has been filed. Whether another local government unit in the National Capital Region has adopted a comparable measure is not sourced. No arrest, charge or case outcome is recorded for the March 2024 killing in Pasig City, and the region has no published count of trans-directed violence against which a single case could be assessed.
